title: Kinase Mobility Shift Assay for Assessing Protein Kinase A Activity
author: Analia G. Novero
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML
materials: Sperm from sexually mature C57BL/6 male mice (10–15 weeks old) Reagents Note: Unless specified, all reagents are stored at room temperature (RT, 20–25 °C).
Bovine serum albumin (BSA) fatty acid-free (Sigma-Aldrich, catalog number: A7906) (4 °C)
cOmplete EDTA-free protease inhibitor cocktail (Roche, catalog number: 4693132001) (4 °C)
Carboxyl-labeled fluorescent Kemptide (sequence LRRASLGK-FITC, termed Kemptide-FITC) (-80 °C) (Biomatik, catalog number:

Note: Additional information on Kemptide-FITC is as follows: Origin: Synthesized by Biomatik. Sequence: N-LRRASLGK-C-(FITC). MW: 1,289.49 Da. Salt form: trifluoroacetate (TFA Salt). Solubility in water: 1 mg/mL. Purity (HPLC): 96.01%. FITC = fluorescein isothiocyanate. Weigh 1 mg of powder and dissolve it in 1 mL of water (do not weigh less than the resolution limit of the scale). Always keep in the dark to avoid quenching of FITC.
Agarose LE (Productos Bio-Lógicos PB-L, catalog number: IB
Source of PKA: recombinant PKA-C (Addgene plasmid, catalog number: 14921, expressed in E. coli BL21 and purified with Ni-NTA resin) or sperm extract (detailed here) Solutions

steps.title: Prepare H‑TYH non‑capacitating medium
steps.instruction: Dissolve NaCl (119.3 mM, 174.3 mg), KCl (4.7 mM, 8.8 mg), CaCl₂·2H₂O (1.71 mM, 6.3 mg), KH₂PO₄ (1.2 mM, 4.1 mg), MgSO₄·7H₂O (1.2 mM, 7.4 mg), HEPES (20 mM, 119.2 mg), and NaOH (5 M) in Milli‑Q water to 25 mL; filter through a 0.45 µm filter; store at 4 °C up to 1 month; on the day of use add 2.2 mg sodium pyruvate and 24.8 mg glucose, then adjust pH to 7.2–7.4 with freshly prepared 5 M NaOH.

steps.title: Prepare CAP 2× capacitating medium
steps.instruction: To 5 mL of H‑TYH medium add NaHCO₃ (40 mM, 16.8 mg) and BSA (10 mg/mL, 50 mg); adjust pH to 7.2–7.4 immediately before use; to obtain capacitating condition mix 1 part CAP 2× with 1 part cells + H‑TYH.

steps.title: Make 1.5× Triton lysis buffer (incomplete)
steps.instruction: Combine 1 M Tris‑HCl pH 7.4 (75 mM, 465.8 µL), 3 M NaCl (225 mM, 465.8 µL), and 100 % Triton X‑100 (1.5 %, 93.1 µL) with distilled water to 5 mL; aliquot 402.5 µL portions; store at –20 °C (one aliquot lyses ~5 cell pellets).

steps.title: Complete 1.5× Triton lysis buffer
steps.instruction: To one 402.5 µL aliquot of incomplete buffer add Roche 50× EDTA‑free protease inhibitor cocktail (15 µL), Roche 10× PhosSTOP (75 µL), and DTT (15 mM, 7.5 µL); keep on ice. DTT should be stored at 2–8 °C and is hygroscopic; use only EDTA‑free inhibitor to avoid chelation of Mg²⁺ in downstream kinase reactions.

steps.title: Make 5× kinase reaction buffer (incomplete)
steps.instruction: Mix 1 M Tris‑HCl pH 7.4 (250 mM, 1363.6 µL) with 1 M MgCl₂ (50 mM, 272.2 µL) and bring to 3 mL with distilled water; aliquot 27.5 µL portions; store at –20 °C. Each aliquot will later be brought to 50 µL for a reaction.

steps.title: Complete 5× kinase reaction buffer
steps.instruction: To each 27.5 µL aliquot of incomplete buffer add ATP (10 mM, 5 µL), DTT (50 mM, 2.5 µL), Roche 50× protease inhibitor cocktail (5 µL, gives 5× final), and Roche 25× PhosSTOP (10 µL, gives 5× final); keep on ice.

steps.title: Prepare 2.5× FITC kinase reaction buffer
steps.instruction: To a 50 µL aliquot of the complete 5× buffer add Kemptide‑FITC (1 mg/mL, 7.75 pmol/µL, 10 µL) and non‑fluorescent Kemptide (1 mg/mL, 7.75 pmol/µL, 10 µL); bring volume to 100 µL with distilled water (38.5 µL); keep on ice and protected from light. This provides an equimolar total substrate concentration of 62 µM (1 µg each substrate = 0.775 nmol).

steps.title: Prepare 10× agarose loading buffer
steps.instruction: Mix glycerol (85–89 % v/v, 740 µL), bromophenol blue (0.8 % w/v, 160 µL), and Tween‑20 (5 % v/v, 50 µL); bring to 1 mL with distilled water; aliquot and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 1× agarose running buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve Tris (1.5 M, 33 mL) in distilled water, adjust pH to 10.0 with 5 M NaOH, then bring to 1 L with water; prepare at least 300 mL (250 mL for tank, 50 mL for gel).

steps.title: Make 1 % agarose LE gel solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1 g agarose LE in 100 mL 50 mM Tris‑HCl pH 10.0; heat until fully dissolved; cool to ~60 °C before pouring into gel tray; insert comb(s) and allow to solidify ~20 min; keep gel covered with running buffer if not used within 40 min (max 2 h at RT).

steps.title: Collect sperm by swim‑out
steps.instruction: Place two epididymides from 10–15‑week‑old C57BL/6 males into 600 µL H‑TYH medium; allow swim‑out to collect sperm cells.

steps.title: Count sperm concentration
steps.instruction: Determine cell concentration using a Neubauer chamber.

steps.title: Calculate lysis buffer volume
steps.instruction: Using the counted total cells, compute the volume of 1.5× Triton lysis buffer needed to obtain 30 × 10⁶ sperm/mL after lysis; note that 10 µL of lysate corresponds to ~300 × 10³ sperm for the kinase reaction (alternative amounts 50–300 × 10³ sperm can be used in a 25 µL reaction).

steps.title: Incubate sperm in experimental media
steps.instruction: Add sperm to the desired condition (non‑capacitating or capacitating) at a suggested ratio of 3 × 10⁶ cells per 400 µL medium; incubate as required.

steps.title: Pellet sperm cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 10 000 × g for 3 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Remove supernatant leaving 30 µL
steps.instruction: Carefully discard 370 µL of supernatant (93 % of 400 µL) so that exactly 30 µL remains; if a different incubation volume was used, adjust the discarded volume to leave 30 µL.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet in cold lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Add cold 1.5× Triton lysis buffer to the pellet to reach a final volume of 100 µL (30 µL supernatant + 70 µL buffer for 3 × 10⁶ sperm). Final 1× buffer composition: 75 mM Tris‑HCl, 150 mM NaCl, 1 % Triton X‑100, 10 mM DTT, 1× EDTA‑free protease inhibitor, 1× PhosSTOP, pH 7.4.

steps.title: Lyse sperm on ice
steps.instruction: Incubate the lysate on ice for 30 min, pipetting up and down every 5 min without creating foam; simultaneously begin preparation of kinase reaction reagents (steps B1–B2).

steps.title: Store sperm extracts
steps.instruction: Keep the clarified sperm extracts on ice; label as “sperm PKA” for later use.

steps.title: Supplement 5× kinase buffer (complete)
steps.instruction: On the day of the experiment add ATP, DTT, protease inhibitor cocktail, and PhosSTOP to each 27.5 µL aliquot of incomplete 5× buffer (as described in step 6) to obtain the complete 5× buffer; keep on ice.

steps.title: Prepare 2.5× FITC reaction buffer
steps.instruction: To the complete 5× buffer add Kemptide and Kemptide‑FITC (see step 7) to generate enough 2.5× FITC buffer for 9–10 reactions; keep on ice and protected from light.

steps.title: Set up kinase reaction tubes
steps.instruction: On ice, for each 25 µL reaction add 10 µL 2.5× FITC buffer, then add sample (recombinant PKA‑C, sperm PKA, or control) in 1–15 µL dH₂O to bring total volume to 25 µL. Optional: add 5 µL of 5 µM cAMP to achieve 1 µM final concentration for positive control. Keep tubes in the dark.

steps.title: Run kinase reaction
steps.instruction: Incubate the tubes at 37 °C for 25 min in the dark.

steps.title: Add loading buffer and denature
steps.instruction: Add 2.8 µL 10× loading buffer (65 % glycerol, 0.8 % bromophenol blue, 5 % Tween‑20) to each tube; heat at 100 °C for 60 s.

steps.title: Clarify reaction products
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 10 000 × g for 1 min at 4 °C; transfer 20 µL supernatant to a fresh tube; store at –20 °C or –80 °C protected from light, or proceed directly to electrophoresis.

steps.title: Assemble agarose gel apparatus
steps.instruction: Prepare 1× agarose running buffer (step 9) and pour the 1 % agarose LE solution (step 10) into the gel tray; insert comb(s) with at least 3 cm spacing; allow to solidify ~20 min; place gel in electrophoresis tank and fill with running buffer.

steps.title: Load samples onto gel
steps.instruction: Load the same volume of each clarified reaction into wells (suggested 4 µL containing 0.4 µg Kemptide‑FITC); load quickly to avoid diffusion; leave an empty well between samples if possible.

steps.title: Run electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Run the gel at 80–100 V until the front exits the gel (~45 min). Protect from intense ambient light; if samples contain high salt, extend run time slightly.

steps.title: Post‑run gel handling
steps.instruction: Remove the gel, place it in a container filled with running buffer to prevent dehydration.

steps.title: Acquire fluorescence image
steps.instruction: Set the gel imager (e.g., Typhoon) to excitation 490 nm, emission 520 nm (or 570–590 nm if signal saturates); adjust PMT sensitivity; acquire image, export as TIFF, and analyze band densitometry with Fiji.

description: Validation of protocol This protocol has been used and validated in the following research article: Novero et al. [1]. A versatile kinase mobility shift assay (KiMSA) for PKA analysis and cyclic AMP detection in sperm physiology (and beyond). Front Cell Dev Biol (Figures 3A and 4A).
